findings.title: duckdb_vector_get_validity return typed uint64 instead of intp, breaking the all-pointers-are-intp contract
findings.description: signatures["duckdb_vector_get_validity"] = uint64(intp) (ducklib.py:237; wrapper ducklib.py:1207-1210). Per duckdb.h the function is `uint64_t *duckdb_vector_get_validity(duckdb_vector vector)` — it returns a POINTER (uint64_t*) to the validity bitmask, not a scalar. numbduck's documented contract is that every pointer is carried as `intp` (CLAUDE.md UDF note 2: '@cfunc signatures must use nb_types.intp (not nb_types.voidptr) because numbduck uses intp for all pointers'; numbox enforces this via _require_intp in meminfo.py). Every other pointer-returning binding follows it — the sibling accessor duckdb_vector_get_data is intp(intp) (ducklib.py:236), and the consumer duckdb_validity_row_is_valid takes the validity pointer as intp (ducklib.py:234, int8(intp, intp), matching duckdb.h `bool duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(uint64_t *validity, idx_t row)`). Only this one pointer return is typed uint64.
findings.impact: In @njit code the returned validity pointer has type uint64, which does not unify with the intp the rest of numbduck (and duckdb_validity_row_is_valid) expects. Callers are forced to insert an explicit intp(...) cast, and omitting it is a numba typing error rather than a silent success — this is exactly what test/test_ducklib.py:1117-1118 must do (`duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(intp(v3_validity_p), intp(0))`), whereas the intp-returning get_vector at line 1111 needs no such cast. A uint64 pointer also does not satisfy numbox helpers that require intp (e.g. _require_intp-guarded paths), and pointer arithmetic over the mask becomes unsigned. Bit pattern is preserved on LP64 (both are 64-bit) so no wrong result occurs on the supported platform; the defect is a real, contract-violating type mismatch and ergonomic/compile-safety hazard, not memory corruption.
findings.recommendation: Change the signature to intp(intp): `signatures["duckdb_vector_get_validity"] = intp(intp)` so the pointer return matches the intp-for-all-pointers convention and unifies with duckdb_validity_row_is_valid without casts. After the change, the intp(...) wrappers in the tests (e.g. test_ducklib.py:1118) become unnecessary.

notes: Scope: numbox contract usage across ducklib.py and pybridge.py, cross-checked against numbox core.proxy.proxy, core.bindings.call (_call_lib_func/_call_lib_func_byval), utils.lowlevel.get_unicode_data_p, and the understanding notes. Items verified sound (no finding): (1) get_unicode_data_p("SELECT 1") in pybridge.py:66 is NOT a dangling-pointer bug — the numba unicode value aliases the CPython str buffer and the "SELECT 1" literal is pinned in extract_connection_ptr.__code__.co_consts, so the borrowed NUL-terminated pointer stays valid across the duckdb_query call. (2) _call_lib_func argument shapes are all correct: every non-byval wrapper passes a tuple (single-arg as (x,), zero-arg as ()), matching the intrinsic's BaseTuple/NoneType handling. (3) _call_lib_func_byval is used for duckdb_fetch_chunk / duckdb_result_return_type / duckdb_result_statement_type passing the 48-byte duckdb_result (UniTuple(intp,6)) by pointer; this is the established, test-exercised numbox helper and I could not obtain duckdb.h to independently adjudicate the by-value-vs-pointer ABI question, and the extensive passing test suite is strong evidence it works on the supported Linux x86-64 target, so it is not flagged. (4) proxy / proxy_if_available semantics (import-time hasattr gating on duckdb_lib, stable cfunc alias, cache anchor) are used correctly. (5) idx_t args typed intp vs uint64 (e.g. duckdb_validity_row_is_valid row arg) are ABI-identical for scalar 64-bit integers and carry small positive values — no correctness impact.
